problem: The cost comparison 'more than single parity but less than a CRC of the same strength' is vague and the direction is wrong: for equal detection strength a CRC needs fewer check bits than two-dimensional parity, and a block of m rows and n columns actually needs m + n + 1 parity bits, not m + n, because of the corner bit.
fix: For an m × n data block the overhead is m + n + 1 parity bits. Two-dimensional parity gives good detection for that many bits, but a CRC using the same number of check bits is stronger, so two-dimensional parity is the cheaper-to-reason-about but weaker option.

problem: The chapter never says the sender must first set the checksum field itself to zero before summing the 16-bit words; a student who sums the header as it stands will compute the wrong value.
fix: Add: at the sender the checksum field is set to 0x0000 before the words are added, and the resulting complement is written into that field.

problem: Step 2 says 'use a 3-bit remainder', but the register values printed in steps 3 and 4 are 4 bits wide (1001 = 9, 1011 = 11). A student may not see why a '3-bit' register holds 9.
fix: Say: keep a 4-bit window; shift the next data bit in at the right, and whenever the leftmost bit of the window is 1, XOR the window with 1011. After the last bit the window holds 000 plus the 3-bit remainder (110).
